newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH HARVARD SAYS MEETS FINMIN DEMANDS FOR FUNDS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH HARVARD SAYS MEETS FINMIN DEMANDS FOR FUNDS.

text.p: Czech investment group Harvard Capital and Consulting (HC&C) on Wednesday said it had fulfilled all Finance Ministry requirements to allow it to open its closed-ended mutual funds.

In mid-January, HC&C said it had applied to the Finance Ministry to transform its closed-end unit trusts into open-end funds in order to "extend investment opportunities" but the ministry rejected the application on March 10 saying unit holders must be protected. It did not elaborate.
But in a statement on Wednesday, Harvard said it had fulfilled the necessary requirements after re-applying to open its funds later in March.
"The second application to open the funds, made on March 13, fulfills all requirements of the ministry," the statement said.
"Claims of improper accounting advertising expenditures from the second wave of voucher privatisation have been fully covered," the statement quoted HC&C Vice-president Boris Ostry as saying.
Finance Ministry officials were not immediately available to comment.

HC&C has said that if the move was approved, it will offer to buy out shareholders from the funds, which were created in the second wave of the government voucher privatisation programme, at a price equal to the net asset value per share.
